description: Reference vectors for the Paradex session grant typed data (EIP-712 and SNIP-12 revision 1), as produced by the Paradex server. Implementations must reproduce every hash byte for byte.
notes: EIP-712 domain: {name: "Paradex Session", version: "1", chainId: signatureChainId (the wallet's current EVM chain)}.
SNIP-12 rev 1 domain: {name: "Paradex Session", version: "1", chainId: paradexChain, revision: "1"}; the message hash account is message.account.
Field order is the order of each type in typedData.types and is frozen.
Hex strings (accounts, keys, nonces) are signed exactly as written: use lowercase 0x hex without leading zeros ("0x0" for none). Nonces are non-zero and at most 128 bits.
Integers are JSON numbers in EIP-712 messages and decimal strings in SNIP-12 messages; both encode the same value.
SNIP-12 string fields must be printable ASCII; markets and scopes are shortstrings of at most 31 characters.
A grant without a builder uses builder {account: "0x0", maxFeeRate: "0", expiresAt: 0}.

Every limit is stated: a positive decimal string, or "none" for no cap (maxLeverage "none" is the market maximum). An empty string is invalid. Builder grants and builder passkeys must give a numeric maxLoss.

markets is non-empty; ["*"] means every market the server permits and must stand alone. Elsewhere * is a wildcard for any run of characters ("*-USD-PERP"), and a pattern must contain a letter or digit and no "**".
A market contains a letter, * or - and does not start with -, 0x, 0b or 0o in either case; symbols are case-sensitive and may contain _ ("kPEPE-USD-PERP", "NEAR-USD-27NOV26-5_4-C").

A mint limit under a numeric ceiling is a number at or below it; under a "none" ceiling it may be anything valid. Each mint market must be listed by the ceiling, matched by a ceiling pattern, or covered by a ["*"] ceiling; a mint pattern is covered only by the same pattern.
SessionMint's WebAuthn challenge is the 32-byte SNIP-12 message hash, base64url-encoded without padding (mintChallenge).
EIP-712 signatures are 65-byte r||s||v with v in {27, 28} and low s. Stark signatures are [r, s] over the SNIP-12 message hash.
The keys below are public test keys: never use them for anything else.
